claims.text: Spark plasma sintering of a powder mixture containing RHEA elements and Cu can produce a large-scale reaction.
Spark plasma sintering can produce a stable, fine-grained RHEA-Cu composite microstructure.
The SPS-produced microstructure mitigates problems caused by the positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
Rapid heating, controlled pressure, and optimized temperature-time profiles are relevant SPS processing features for this RHEA-Cu composite.
Sintering under an inert atmosphere with optimized thermal and pressure parameters induces rapid reaction and densification.
The proposed SPS conditions minimize diffusion-driven phase segregation.
The resulting microstructure has a fine grain size.
The resulting microstructure has limited phase separation at interfaces between the HEA matrix and Cu-rich regions.
Rapid heating and high pressure accelerate reaction kinetics.
Rapid heating and high pressure promote homogeneous mixing of the RHEA and Cu constituents.
Rapid SPS processing suppresses extensive diffusion.
Extensive diffusion would enhance segregation because of the large positive heat of mixing between the refractory elements and Cu.
The SPS-processed composite will have an integrated and stable microstructure.
The SPS-processed composite will show improved thermal stability.
The SPS-processed composite will show improved irradiation resistance.
The SPS-processed composite will maintain large-scale reaction uniformity.
Conventional sintering entails prolonged high-temperature exposure that leads to phase segregation and unstable microstructures.
The microstructural benefits of SPS may diminish when temperature, pressure, or sintering time are not tailored to the particular RHEA-Cu system.
